features.title: Print a phone sign-in QR for a trusted HTTPS origin
features.summary: At startup the Host runs a loopback rewrite proxy so a TLS-terminating tunnel (Tailscale Serve) can reach the native listener without a trustedHosts setting, detects the tailnet hostname, points Serve at that proxy, and prints one scannable sign-in QR. Configured https origins skip detection.
failureModes: A non-HTTPS, credentialed, or non-absolute origin is ignored instead of printed.
A busy proxy port is reported on the terminal and leaves the rest of DSH running.
Missing Tailscale, or Serve failing to start, prints no auto-detected QR and never guesses an origin.

A phone that opens the origin signed out gets a sign-in page naming the terminal QR and any claimer's sign-in link (phone-pairing's Pair this phone), not the native listener's bare 401; API requests keep their 401.

verification.reason: The Host prints to the terminal and renders no UI; the scratch Host boot check verifies the bundle loads and prints.

features.title: Share the phone origin with other Host plugins
features.summary: The edge API (`@dshfiles/phone-access/edge-api`) reports whether the proxy listens and which public origins reach it, and lets a Host plugin claim paths and a cookie on that origin. Claimed requests go to the claimer's loopback port unchanged; the rest still reach the native listener. Phone pairing uses it to serve /pair and paired devices on the same tailnet address instead of repointing Tailscale.
features.currentSurface: host: dshx API phone-access-edge (status, claimRoutes, releaseRoutes)
failureModes: A browser Client or the agent cannot claim routes; only a Host plugin caller can, and only its own package's claim.
With the proxy not listening, status says so and a claimer falls back to its own route.

verification.testName: sends claimed requests to the claimer unchanged and every other request to DSH with the loopback Host
keeps one route claim per package and reports it until it is released
lets only a Host plugin claim phone routes

verification.reason: A Host-to-Host API with no UI; the forwarding test drives real HTTP through the proxy, and phone-pairing's access tests cover the claimer that uses it.
